'''Sarah Trimpin''' is a German/American<ref name="Waters">{{cite web |url=https://www.waters.com/waters/en_US/Professor-Sarah-Trimpin%2C-Wayne-State-University/nav.htm?locale=en_US&cid=134780080 |title=Professor Sarah Trimpin, Wayne State University : Waters |format= |accessdate=2020-01-29 |archive-date=2020-07-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200702171321/https://www.waters.com/waters/en_US/Professor-Sarah-Trimpin,-Wayne-State-University/nav.htm?locale=en_US&cid=134780080 |url-status=dead }}</ref> chemist and Professor at the [[Wayne State University]].<ref name="labPage">{{cite web |url=http://www.chem.wayne.edu/faculty/trimpin/ |title=www.chem.wayne.edu |format= |accessdate=2020-01-29}}</ref> Her research interests revolve around ionizing methods in [[mass spectrometry]]. Her work has resulted in the formation of a company (MSTM, LLC) which aims to bring advanced ionization methods to industry. Her work has been recognized by the [[American Society for Mass Spectrometry]] with the Research Award in 2010,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Research Awards |url=https://www.asms.org/about-asms-awards/research-awards |access-date=2022-12-27 |website=www.asms.org}}</ref> and the [[Biemann Medal]] in 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Biemann Medal |url=https://www.asms.org/about-asms-awards/biemann-medal |access-date=2022-12-27 |website=www.asms.org}}</ref>

Trimpin received her undergraduate training at the [[Universität Konstanz]] in Germany in 1999 and her PhD from the [[Max Planck Institute for Polymer Research]] in 2002 ([[Mainz]]).<ref name="labPage"/> After postdoctoral work at [[Oregon State University]] and [[Indiana University]], she joined the faculty at Wayne State University in 2008.<ref name="Waters"/>
